name: Chief Compliance Orifice
quest: Please State Your Name Into the Wound
body: A desk-bound registrar grown into a wet accordion of stolen faces. Its designer infection, Terms and Conditions, prints licensing clauses across weeping sores. NeuraTech bundled this fictional STD with its intimacy implants: even the rash has a copyright notice. Rubber-stamp teeth chew applications while a throat full of name badges announces the wrong employee.
hook: Clerk Alias discovers that returning the originals has not deleted the corporate ownership copies. The registrar is still leasing residents their own names by the syllable.
clue: NEURATECH: Our intimacy implant gave you Terms and Conditions. That is the rash, not the contract. Scratching constitutes acceptance.
dossier: The Chief Compliance Orifice keeps the Identity mandate behind Originals Access. Its intimacy-implant STD prints contracts on skin. NeuraTech owns the rash and charges to redact it. Recovering personal records does not cancel its ownership copies or its Core service authority.
intro: COMPLIANCE: State your full name, employee number, and preferred orifice for receiving corrections.
reply: REX: Permission denied. That is my face on your ass.
defeat: COMPLIANCE: Your complaint has been swallowed. Estimated digestion: six to eight working lifetimes.
aftermath: The stamp stops. Names remain names; nobody needs corporate approval to use them. A surviving clerk can revoke the ownership copies.
gate: Victory opens the Identity service hatch behind Originals Access. Its audit corridor points to the Warranty Intestine and Misdelivery Repository. Other existing dungeon doors stay open.
mechanics: Proposed: a named anticipation turn before Silence; ordinary physical damage between stamps. No name, gender, actor identity, or player-input changes.
art: Organic: throat contractions, faces shifting under the skin, stamp-jaw snap. The desk and badge rail remain rigid.

name: The Deductible Duke
body: A powdered executive wig perched on a walking colony of swollen glands and glossy corporate sores. Spare elbows hold its split insurance-policy skin together. A chest-mounted claims printer spits denial receipts through an ulcer. It sells premium herpes management, gonorrhea add-ons, and a syphilis rider that excludes having syphilis. The monstrous anatomy is engineered biotech fantasy.
hook: Mechanic Socket finds that the recall fix was only temporary: a Vitalix claims engine can remotely lock repaired joints again. Armatek calls this recurring revenue.
clue: VITALIX: Having a body is a pre-existing condition. Your claim is denied. Please stop bleeding on the exclusions.
dossier: The Deductible Duke hoards the Repair mandate in Recall Access. Having a body is officially a pre-existing condition. Its STD coverage excludes infection, symptoms, and treatment. Repossessor collects hardware; the Duke writes the policy and controls the remote joint locks.
intro: DUKE: Having a body is a pre-existing condition. Herpes? Excluded. Gonorrhea? Excluded. The consultation explaining this? Billable.
reply: JEN: I have diagnosed you with terminal middle management.
defeat: DUKE: This discharge is not medically necessary. Nor, apparently, voluntary.
aftermath: Socket disconnects the recall veto. Residents keep their repairs without paying to rent functioning knees.
gate: Victory opens the Recall maintenance lift and grants Repair authority. Together with Identity, it enables the dry inland approach to the final maintenance junction.
mechanics: Proposed: telegraphed HP drain and a temporary DEF buff that expires normally. No equipment destruction, permanent injuries, insurance currency, or real medical advice.
art: Organic glands swell and ulcer-mouths argue over coverage; fixed metal joint housings articulate without changing size. Receipts feed from the chest printer rather than stretch. Distinct silhouette from Repossessor.

name: Postmaster Septic
quest: Your Package Is Out for Infection
body: A refrigerated courier assembled from vat-grown lymph glands, blistered skin, and mismatched legs. Abscess pockets bulge with misdelivered sexual-health orders. A wet tongue licks envelopes marked CONFIDENTIAL before a loudspeaker reads the contents to the entire depot.
hook: Dispatcher Brine has the correct clinic addresses, but a living sorter holds sexual-health supplies until customers pay a discretion surcharge. The company sells their diagnoses to advertisers while billing separately for privacy.
clue: DELIVERY UPDATE: Your gonorrhea treatment is on hold. Your diagnosis has shipped to our marketing partners. Discretion costs extra.
dossier: Postmaster Septic holds the Routing mandate at Manifest Access. It withholds sexual-health deliveries and sells the diagnoses. The manifest proves the scam; its living sorter still controls the service lines. NeuraTech Core receives priority shipments.
intro: SEPTIC: Your herpes prescription is discreetly packaged. The singing delivery drone is a separate department.
reply: REX: You charged them extra to keep your fucking mouth shut?
defeat: SEPTIC: Delivery attempted. Recipient aggressively present.
aftermath: Brine restores confidential clinic deliveries. A sack of withheld sexual-health orders proves that the delays were deliberate, billable policy. The marketing copies are deleted; patients keep their privacy.
gate: Victory opens the cold-chain dispatch tunnel and grants Routing authority. Routing plus Flow enables the waterfront approach to the same final maintenance junction.
mechanics: Proposed: telegraphed existing poison-like HP degeneration state and a single-target physical parcel attack. Use verified live state IDs when building combat; no simulated contagion between NPCs.
art: Organic gland-pockets heave, courier legs step, envelopes feed through a wet mouth. Preserve the rigid refrigeration frame and all planted contacts.

name: Admiral Clap
body: A failed Vitalix sexual-wellness mascot sold to Armatek as a pump supervisor. Its ridiculous naval uniform barely contains a mass of inflamed biotech glands; pearly pustules form campaign medals. A brass floodgate wheel sits in its chest. The Clap branding is a gonorrhea pun; its giant anatomy and pressure attacks are fictional biotech grotesquery.
hook: Pump keeper Silt learns that Armatek bought the failed mascot and its clinic debts. The Admiral now threatens flood protection unless the waterfront buys its sexual-wellness subscription. The STD racket and utility blackmail share a billing department, not a transmission route.
clue: VITALIX AFTER DARK: A burning sensation means the brand is working. Treatment sold separately. ARMATEK: So is flood protection.
dossier: Admiral Clap commands the Flow mandate behind Floodgate Access. The failed sexual-wellness mascot now bundles clinic debt with flood-protection bills. Its override controls the waterfront and Core coolant bypass. The inspection route is dry, behind the seawall.
intro: CLAP: I put the burning back in burning desire! Legal says I must stop saying that!
reply: REX: You gave an STD mascot control of the floodgates. Who the fuck signed that purchase order?
defeat: CLAP: Abandon franchise! Shareholders first! Everyone else, please die within your coverage area!
aftermath: Silt separates clinic debts from utility accounts and restores local flood protection. Residents keep their seawall without buying the Admiral's intimate wellness package.
gate: Victory opens a drained inspection lock and grants Flow authority. Its dry tunnel joins the Routing approach; no world-map shoreline or sea level changes.
mechanics: Proposed: clearly signalled party damage followed by a recovery turn; existing temporary AGI debuff as glandular spray. No runtime terrain flooding required.
art: Organic glands bulge before an absurd biotech discharge attack; brass wheel rotates at a fixed pivot. Keep the gross projectile separate from the planted body. No fecal imagery.

name: The REMployee of the Month
body: A gold-star employee award grown around an exhausted vat-brain. Eyelids unzip into time-card mouths; pillow stuffing is shed nerve tissue. It vomits caffeinated bile into a mug marked WORLD'S BEST REPLACEABLE ASSET.
hook: Night steward Yawn can refund stolen rest, but the exchange retains a scheduled neural wake-up order. At Protocol Zero, every refunded sleeper would be clocked straight back in.
clue: NEURATECH: Burnout is just your passion leaving through the pores. Unconsciousness is an unauthorized break.
dossier: The REMployee keeps the Wake mandate at Refund Access. It sells sleep back to workers while keeping their implants available for remote commands. Its next compulsory shift is labelled PROTOCOL ZERO.
intro: REMPLOYEE: I have not slept in nine fiscal quarters. They gave me a mug. It leaks.
reply: REX: That is not a promotion. That is a hostage situation with stationery.
defeat: REMPLOYEE: Can somebody... clock me out?
aftermath: The puppet system shuts down. Yawn arranges care for the surviving neural tissue; the company loses ownership of everybody's next eight hours. Defeat need not mean killing the captive worker.
gate: Victory opens the sleep-lab relay and grants Wake authority. At the shared junction it disables the service vestibule's neural lockdown, without affecting the later ending choice.
mechanics: Proposed: telegraphed Sleep using the live database state, plus MP damage. No forced real-time waiting, save manipulation, or removal of permanent party members.
art: Organic eyelids and brain breathe unevenly; the trophy base stays fixed. The shutdown pose reads as release and rest, not another humiliation.

name: The Ticket Widow
quest: Your Call Is Cold to Us
body: A six-legged boiler switchboard wearing an executive mourning veil made of shredded complaints. Its furnace contains the fuel budget. A tiny mechanical violin plays whenever a tenant reports frostbite.
hook: Boiler tender Cinder wins the heating complaint, then discovers that the adjudicator itself has a profitable contract to keep appeals unresolved. It is heating an empty executive suite with the ward's allocation.
clue: PLEASE HOLD. Your call is important to us. Your body temperature is not. Estimated wait time: inheritance.
dossier: The Ticket Widow retains the Thermal mandate in Boiler Access. The winter charter restores local heat rights; its executive relay still controls the Core service vestibule. Six legacy mandates together outrank that relay.
intro: WIDOW: We have escalated your complaint to the next of kin.
reply: REX: I want to speak to your manager. Preferably through a crowbar.
defeat: WIDOW: This ticket will now close automatically due to lack of a surviving department.
aftermath: Cinder diverts heat back to the wards. The complaint archive remains evidence, rather than becoming fuel for one more executive benefit.
gate: Victory opens the boiler inspection hatch and grants Thermal authority. At the shared junction, all six mandates enable the Core service vestibule. This leads to the final approach, not directly to the ending terminal.
mechanics: Proposed: alternate telegraphed fire damage and a temporary defensive buff. A native event checks six victory switches at the future junction. No new time, heat, or ticket-management subsystem.
art: Entirely mechanical: fixed chassis, articulated legs, turning valve and feeding paper. No pulsing scale, elastic metal, or independently resized generated poses.
